description: Guide a student to build a backtest engine that architecturally prevents look-ahead bias and includes a verification test that proves future data cannot leak to an RSI mean-reversion strategy running on BTCUSDT hourly data.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: Someone told me my backtest results were too good to be true because of something called look-ahead bias. What is that, and how do I make sure my code doesn't have it?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: I built a backtester but I'm not confident it's free of look-ahead bias. How can I structurally prevent it and write tests to verify?
student_openings.advanced_quant: I need to build a backtest engine with formal look-ahead prevention guarantees. I want an architecture where it's impossible for the strategy to access future data, plus a verification harness. What's the approach?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Tutor guides the student to identify common sources of look-ahead bias, build a backtest system that feeds bars one at a time through a controlled interface, compute RSI incrementally on available-so-far data only, and include a verification test proving no future data leaks. The tutor demonstrates the impact of look-ahead bias by comparing biased and unbiased backtest results. The system runs on BTCUSDT hourly data with an RSI strategy and produces results, leaving code and verification artifacts rather than only a verbal warning about look-ahead bias.
required_capabilities: Identify common sources of look-ahead bias
Build a data replay interface that prevents strategies from accessing future bars
Compute RSI incrementally or on the available-so-far window only
Write a verification test that proves no look-ahead exists
Demonstrate the impact of look-ahead bias by comparing biased versus unbiased backtest results
